name: Patchimon v1 - Grey-Box Avatar
description: 3D Monster Pair Programming Companion for Kiro IDE. Stitches three incompatible technologies: 3D generation pipeline + VS Code Extension Host APIs + Webview 3D Scene (Three.js)

requirements.title: Extension Infrastructure
requirements.description: TypeScript VS Code extension targeting Kiro IDE with webview panel integration
acceptance_criteria: Extension activates on command: 'Patchimon: Show Avatar'
Webview panel displays in sidebar
Zero external setup required (no API keys, GPU, accounts)
Works completely offline

requirements.title: Avatar System
requirements.description: Single preset monster avatar with segmented body parts and patch colors
acceptance_criteria: Classic Patch-Plush design with 7 segmented parts
Color scheme: mint, lavender, mustard, dusty pink patches
Three.js renderer displays avatar in webview
Design principle: 'the seams are the joints'

requirements.title: Animation System
requirements.description: Three procedural animation states with parts-and-pivots approach
acceptance_criteria: Idle animation: breathing sway + bolt twitch
Celebrate animation: arms up + hop motion
Flinch animation: squash down + arms cover face
No skeletal animation required
Smooth transitions via requestAnimationFrame

requirements.title: Editor Reaction System
requirements.description: Monitor VS Code diagnostics and file events to trigger avatar reactions
acceptance_criteria: Flinch triggers when error diagnostics appear
Celebrate triggers when errors clear after existing
File save shows acknowledgment in idle state
No chat or LLM features

requirements.title: Kiroween 2026 Compliance
requirements.description: Meet all hackathon hard rules and requirements
acceptance_criteria: Spec-first development: spec committed before code
/.kiro directory at repo root, never gitignored
MIT license file at repo root
No absolute local paths in any files
All references use repo-relative paths only
No third-party monster-franchise trademarks

requirements.title: Technical Constraints
requirements.description: Architecture and technical requirements for extension
acceptance_criteria: Three.js WebGL renderer with proper CSP
CSP allows blob: and data: for img-src/connect-src
Extension packages as VSIX for judge installation
Works on fresh Kiro install with no setup
Credit budget ~900 Kiro credits

requirements.title: Performance
acceptance_criteria: Webview loads and renders avatar within 2 seconds
Animation transitions within 200ms of trigger
Minimal CPU usage during idle animation

design.architecture: Three-tier system: Extension Host (Node.js) <-> Message Bridge <-> Webview (Browser/Three.js)

components.name: Extension Entry Point
components.responsibility: Activation, command registration, webview provider initialization, diagnostics monitor setup

components.name: Webview Provider
components.responsibility: Webview lifecycle management, HTML generation with CSP, message bridge, Three.js scene setup

components.name: Diagnostics Monitor
components.responsibility: Editor event listening, error state tracking, animation command translation

components.name: Avatar Renderer
components.responsibility: Three.js scene, grey-box geometry, procedural animation, message handling

components.name: Animation Controller
components.responsibility: State machine, procedural transforms, requestAnimationFrame loop

critical_decisions.rationale: GLTFLoader fetches embedded textures from blob: URLs. Without img-src/connect-src allowing blob:/data:, models render grey with no error.
Test reaction loop with simple geometry before investing in 3D asset generation. Order: extension shell + grey-box reactions FIRST, real assets SECOND.
No skeletal animation needed for non-humanoid. Segmented parts with 'seams are joints' principle allows procedural animation.
